correctness.rationale: The group algebra K[X^±1,Y^±1]/(X^m−1,Y^n−1) splits into length-(2^a,2^b) root-pair local algebras. P=X+X^-1+Y+Y^-1 has vanishing constant term iff η=ζ or ζ^-1, giving 2g−1 pairs. Nontrivial root pairs permit invertible coordinate changes U=f(X)−f(ζ),V=f(Y)−f(η), and multiplication by U+V has k uniform chains length L by Frobenius. At (1,1), f(1+u)=u²/(1+u), P^(L/2)=0; the quotient by P is free rank two over K[v]/(v^k), giving 2k blocks and forcing length L/2. Fitting decomposition then gives cumulative kernel c(t), sharp time and counts Q^(d+c(t)). Independently reconstructed binary Cayley adjacency and compared 570 nontrivial kernel ranks (distinct from open-square comparisons below); no finite test was treated as an all-size proof.

final_claim: Every m,n>=3 characteristic-two four-neighbor torus has zero-primary Jordan partition (1)^(2g-1) for L=1 or (L/2)^(2k) + L^(2(g-1)k) for L>=2, with exact Fitting entrance-time populations over every finite field F_Q.
limitations: Characteristic-two finite fields only, open-neighbor C_m×C_n with m,n>=3; no primitive period census on invertible Fitting component.
